result.proposed_fix: Replace the regex-plus-string approach in evaluate.numbers with a numeral tokenizer that has an explicit invariant: each numeral is either parsed whole into one canonical value or reported as unparseable. Accept optional sign (-, −, U+2212, 'minus'); integer part as western grouping \d{1,3}(,\d{3})+, Indian grouping \d{1,2}(,\d{2})*,\d{3}, space/NBSP/thin-space/narrow-NBSP grouping \d{1,3}([ \u00a0\u2009\u202f]\d{3})+, or a bare digit run; optional .fraction. Strip separators, parse to Decimal, apply sign and existing _SCALE/_UNIT, and emit a normalised canonical string (so 1000.5 == 1000.50). Return a sentinel for numerals that cannot be read cleanly: verify should drop the claim (NUMBER_NOT_IN_CITED_SOURCE / unverifiable) and find_conflicts should not use subset suppression to rule out a conflict for that pair. Add property-style regressions in tests/web covering each grouping style, sign variant and decimal-normalisation case in both verify and find_conflicts, in both directions (5,00,000 vs 5,00,00,000; 1 000 000 vs 1 500 000; -3.2% vs 3.2%; −3.2% vs 3.2%; 1,000.5 vs 1,000.50 kept), plus an invariant test that numbers() never yields a value that is a digit-substring fragment of a longer grouped numeral.
result.root_cause: uri_web/evaluate.py:19 _NUMBER is a single ad-hoc regex that only knows western 3-digit comma grouping (\d{1,3}(,\d{3})+) or bare digit runs, and captures no sign. Any other numeral (Indian lakh/crore grouping 5,00,000, space/NBSP-grouped thousands 1 000 000, leading -/− sign) is silently split into fragments ('5','00000' / '5','00','00000') or loses its sign, and numbers() (evaluate.py:69-80) returns those fragments as if they were values, compared as raw strings. Both consumers then use set-subset comparisons — verify keeps a claim when claim_nums <= source_nums (synthesize.py:99), and find_conflicts skips any pair where one set is a subset of the other (evaluate.py:162) — so a fragmented smaller amount is usually a subset of the larger amount's fragments and the check fails open (5 lakh vs 5 crore KEPT, 0 conflicts). The tokenizer has no 'whole numeral or unparseable' invariant, and the comparators trust its output.
result.why_earlier_repairs_failed: Each repair patched only the literal example strings of the latest finding. Repair 1 (16f75d8) changed only the lookbehind (?<![\w.]) -> (?<!\d) and tested exactly Rs.500/approx.900/No.5 (tests/web/test_w1_r1_review_regressions.py). Repair 4 (52e852d) bolted unit/scale suffix handling (_SCALE/_UNIT/_fmt) onto group 2 for R4-02, leaving the integer-grouping alternative, sign handling and the subset-based comparators unchanged, and tested only the reviewer's magnitude-word pairs ($5bn vs $5m, 2 crore vs 2 lakh). Repairs 2 and 3 (627f6b9, 1615512) did not touch uri_web. No repair added a test that every numeral is extracted whole, or covered fragmentation against the subset rules, so the 36 existing R1-01/R4-02 regressions pass at HEAD while R5-01 reproduces.
